title: break & continue
learningGoals: use `break` to leave a loop early
use `continue` to skip the rest of one iteration
trace a loop that uses both
know that `break` leaves only the innermost loop, and use a flag to leave two

youtube.title: break vs continue: Exit or Skip? | C Programming EP 29
youtube.description: Sometimes you need to leave a loop early, or skip just one round. break is the emergency exit, continue is the skip button. We trace both line by line and fix the classic "break only left one loop" bug. 0:00 Challenge answer and hook 0:25 break: the emergency exit 1:05 continue: the skip button 1:35 Both together, line by line 3:25 Bug of the Day: break in the wrong loop 4:55 Challenge

scenes.onScreen: EP 28 challenge: chai menu run with 1, 5, 3
scenes.animation: Typing SFX; then a fire alarm rings over a looping track
scenes.narration: Last challenge: a chai shop menu with do-while. Show the menu, read a choice, print a message, and repeat while choice is not 3. Here it is running: 1, chai coming. 5, not on the menu. 3, bye. Now imagine you are running laps at Campal ground and the fire alarm rings. You don't finish your laps. You leave right now. C has a keyword for that.

scenes.onScreen: Loop track with a red EXIT door: `break` jumps straight out
scenes.animation: Xecxec runs laps, hits break, exits through door; door slam SFX
scenes.narration: The word break, followed by a semicolon, means: leave this loop immediately. Don't run the rest of the body. Don't check the condition again. Jump to the first line after the loop's closing brace. You met break once already, in the switch statement. Same keyword, same idea: get out.

scenes.onScreen: Same track: `continue` jumps from mid-lap back to the check
scenes.animation: Xecxec skips a hurdle via a shortcut arrow; whoosh
scenes.narration: continue is gentler. It means: skip the rest of this round, and go to the next one. In a for loop, it jumps to the update, then the check. In a while loop, it jumps straight to the check. The loop keeps going. Only this one round is cut short.

scenes.animation: Inputs 4, -3, 6, 0 drop in; skipped line greys out on continue; break arrow flies past the brace
scenes.narration: Let's use both. [HL 4] int num, to hold the user's number. [HL 6] for i from 1 to 5. Up to five numbers. [TRACK i=1] [HL 7] [HL 8] Ask for number 1, and read it. The user types 4. [TRACK num=4] [HL 10] if num equals 0. No. [HL 14] if num less than 0. No. [HL 18] Print "Square = 16". Next round. [TRACK i=2] The user types minus 3. [TRACK num=-3] Is it 0? No. [HL 14] Is it less than 0? Yes. [HL 15] Print "Negative, skipped." [HL 16] continue. So we skip line eighteen, no square, and go straight to i plus plus. [TRACK i=3] The user types 6. [TRACK num=6] Square = 36. [TRACK i=4] Now the user types 0. [TRACK num=0] [HL 10] num equals 0, yes. [HL 11] Print "Stopping early." [HL 12] break. We leave the loop right now. i was only 4. The fifth number is never asked. [HL 21] We land on "Loop over."
Run it with 4, minus 3, 6 and 0. Square 16. Negative, skipped. Square 36. Stopping early. Loop over. Exactly as we traced.

scenes.animation: Xecxec in a traffic police hat, whistle SFX
scenes.narration: Why did the loop get a ticket from the traffic police? It took a break in the middle of the road.

scenes.animation: Multiples of 3 fade out from a number strip
scenes.narration: A quick one. For i from 1 to 20, if i mod 3 equals 0, continue. Otherwise print i. Mod 3 equals 0 means "divisible by 3". So 3, 6, 9 and the rest are skipped. We get 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8 and so on up to 20.

scenes.onScreen: `brkbug.c` nested search: break leaves only the inner loop; fix with a `found` flag
scenes.animation: Butter frame; two nested tracks; break exits inner track only, outer keeps running (Tomato); fix shows flag flipping to 1 then second break
scenes.narration: Today's bug catches almost everyone. We search a 3 by 3 grid for the cell at row 2, column 2. When we find it, we break. Run it. We see 1 comma 1, 1 comma 2, 1 comma 3, 2 comma 1, "Found it!"... and then 3 comma 1, 3 comma 2, 3 comma 3. The search kept going! Why? break only leaves the loop it is directly inside. Here that is the inner col loop. The outer row loop simply moves on to row 3. The fix: use a flag. Before the loops, int found equals 0. When we find it, set found to 1, then break the inner loop. Right after the inner loop, inside the outer one, check: if found, break again. Now the output stops right after "Found it!". No compiler error helps you here. You have to know the rule.

scenes.onScreen: Rules card: break = leave loop, continue = next round, both only affect the innermost loop
scenes.narration: Two rules to remember. break leaves the loop. continue jumps to the next round. And both work only on the innermost loop they are inside. Use them when they make code clearer, not to patch messy logic.

scenes.onScreen: "Print 1 to 30, skip multiples of 4, stop at the first number above 25 divisible by 7" and Next: EP 30
scenes.narration: Your challenge: loop i from 1 to 30. Skip any number divisible by 4, using continue. And stop the whole loop, using break, at the first number greater than 25 that is divisible by 7. Print each number that survives. Next episode: nested loops, loops inside loops. Keep coding, says Xecxec!

bug.error:
No compiler error. Wrong output (the search continues into row 3):

(1,1) (1,2) (1,3) (2,1) Found it!
(3,1) (3,2) (3,3) 
Search finished.
bug.why: `break` exits only the innermost loop, so a flag is needed to stop the outer loop too.

shorts.title: The Fire Alarm Rings Mid-Loop
shorts.hook: Xecxec running laps, alarm bell rings
shorts.script: You're running laps. The fire alarm rings. You don't finish your laps, you leave now. In C, that's break. One word, and your loop is over, right there. Full episode on Koding Konkani.
shorts.caption: The emergency exit for loops.

shorts.title: break vs continue in 30 Seconds
shorts.script: break and continue. break leaves the loop completely and jumps past the closing brace. continue skips only the rest of this round and moves to the next one. Exit versus skip. And both only affect the innermost loop.
shorts.caption: Never mix them up again.

shorts.title: Why Didn't break Stop My Search?
shorts.hook: "Found it!" then more output keeps printing
shorts.script: We found the cell and called break. But the program kept searching row 3. Why? break only leaves the loop it's directly inside, the inner one. The outer loop carried on. Fix: set a found flag, and check it after the inner loop to break again.
shorts.onScreen: FOUND IT... AND KEPT GOING? / break = 1 LOOP ONLY / USE A FLAG
shorts.caption: The nested-loop break trap.
